abstract: Quantum error correction provides a route to realizing large-scale quantum computation but incurs substantial resource overheads. Here we highlight recent advances that reduce these overheads by co-designing different levels of the computational stack, including algorithms, quantum-error-correction strategies and hardware architecture. We then discuss opportunities for further optimization such as leveraging flexible qubit connectivity and quantum low-density parity check codes. These strategies can bring useful quantum computation closer to reality as experiments advance in the coming years.
